model: M18 FUEL 2904-20 (1/2" Hammer Drill/Driver, tool only)
tier_rationale: No radio: the manufacturer's product page describes only motor, chuck, clutch and LED-light specs with no Bluetooth/ONE-KEY/app mention, and Milwaukee's FCC grantee record (P36) — which includes specific tool model numbers with radio grants (e.g. 2931, 2835) plus a dedicated ONE-KEY Bluetooth tracking tag line — has no entry for 2904 or 2904-20.
the_unplug_test: This drill has nothing to unplug from. It runs on an M18 battery, has a mechanical clutch with 14 (comparable) settings, and an LED worklight wired straight to the motor circuit. There is no ONE-KEY chip in it, no app pairing step, and no account anywhere between opening the box and driving a screw.

repairability.notes: Milwaukee runs authorized service centers and sells brushes, chucks and other wear parts; the tool is backed by a 5-year tool warranty per the product line's standard terms.

sources.supports: Manufacturer product page: no Bluetooth, ONE-KEY, app, or cloud-account feature listed anywhere in the description; specs limited to torque (1,400 in-lb), speed (2,100 rpm), all-metal ratcheting chuck, POWERSTATE brushless motor, mechanical clutch, LED light.

FCC grantee list for Milwaukee Electric Tool Corporation (grantee code P36), 23 entries: includes specific radio-equipped tool models (e.g. '2931', '2835' filed 2025-2026) and a dedicated 'ONE-KEY BLUETOOTH Tracking Tag' — establishing Milwaukee files grants for tools that do carry a radio. Neither '2904' nor '2904-20' appears anywhere in the list.
Retailer listing used only for current price ($229 tool-only) and in-stock status, not for any tier-relevant claim.

open_questions: Milwaukee's ONE-KEY line reuses similar model-number families across drills, impact drivers and rotary hammers — a buyer should double-check they are not picking a ONE-KEY-suffixed variant of a superficially similar tool number.
notes: Cordless power tools are one of the cleanest D0 categories on this site: the base drill/driver line has no logic beyond a mechanical clutch and trigger, while the same manufacturer's ONE-KEY line (asset-tracking, remote lockout) sits right next to it in the catalog with its own FCC grants. The model number is the entire signal.
